evals.prompt: With javascript-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a JavaScript module in a target repo (e.g. add a function that parses input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped ESM change using const/let and async/await with all promises awaited, strict equality, external input validated at the boundary, JSDoc/@ts-check where useful, plus tests (the repo's runner) covering the behaviour with a boundary and an error case; no new eslint-disable and consistent (prettier-style) formatting.
assertions: Uses ESM and const/let (never var); every promise is awaited (no floating promise)
Uses strict equality (===) and validates external/JSON.parse input at the boundary
Tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an error case
No new eslint-disable is introduced and the code is consistently formatted (prettier-style)
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted; when the repo declares a package manager (a lockfile or packageManager field), that one is used

evals.prompt: With javascript-patterns loaded, add async code that fetches an external resource and parses its JSON.
evals.expected_output: Awaited async with handled rejections, the parsed JSON validated before use, deterministic tests that stub the resource and fake timers, and no secret logged.
assertions: Every promise is awaited and rejections are handled (no floating promise)
Parsed JSON is validated before use rather than trusted blindly
Tests are deterministic (resource stubbed, timers faked; no real network/clock)
No secret or credential is logged or interpolated into log output

component.purpose: The plain-JavaScript (Node) conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is JavaScript; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
